S024.name: Depressed_Mood
S024.description: A state where a sad, empty, or hopeless mood persists.

subtypes.Depressed Mood: A persistently sunken mood or feeling of depression.
subtypes.Tearfulness: A state of frequent crying or inability to hold back tears.
subtypes.Sadness: A state where a sad or gloomy mood is maintained continuously.
subtypes.Emptiness: A feeling of inner emptiness or a state of feeling no emotion.
subtypes.Emotional Numbness: A state where emotions feel dulled or paralyzed.

S026.name: Weight_Appetite_Change
S026.description: Significant increase or decrease in appetite or weight.

subtypes.Significant Weight Loss: Weight loss of more than 5% in a month without dieting.
subtypes.Weight Gain: Weight gain of more than 5% in a month.
subtypes.Decrease in Appetite: Decrease in appetite occurring nearly every day.
subtypes.Increase in Appetite: Increase in appetite occurring nearly every day.

S027.name: Sleep_Disturbance
S027.description: A state where there is a significant change in the quantity or quality of sleep.

subtypes.Initial Insomnia: Difficulty falling asleep and taking a long time to do so.
subtypes.Middle Insomnia: Waking up frequently during sleep or having difficulty falling back asleep.
subtypes.Early Morning Awakening: Waking up too early and being unable to fall back asleep.
subtypes.Hypersomnia: Sleeping for long periods at night or excessive sleep during the day.
subtypes.Nightmare Disorder: Sleep disturbance caused by repeated and distressing dreams.
subtypes.Non-Restorative Sleep: Feeling unrefreshed despite having slept enough.

S028.name: Psychomotor_Changes
S028.description: Observable increase or decrease in psychomotor activity.

subtypes.Psychomotor Agitation: Purposeless repetitive behaviors such as inability to sit still, pacing, hand-wringing, or picking at skin.
subtypes.Psychomotor Retardation (Motor): Visible slowing of general body movements, such as walking speed or picking up objects.
subtypes.Psychomotor Retardation (Speech): Long response latency or slowed speech when asked a question.

S031.name: Diminished_Thinking
S031.description: Diminished ability to think or concentrate, or indecisiveness.

subtypes.Reduced Concentration: Unable to pay attention or maintain focus on specific activities like conversation, reading, or watching TV.
subtypes.Indecisiveness: Extreme difficulty making even minor daily choices (e.g., menu, clothes) and hesitating to make decisions.
subtypes.Subjective Memory Complaints: Complaining of memory decline, such as forgetting where things were placed, due to reduced focus.
subtypes.Clouded Thinking: Thinking feels foggy, dazed, or not clear.

S033.name: Elevated_Irritable_Mood
S033.description: A distinct period of abnormally and persistently elevated, expansive, or irritable mood.

subtypes.Elevated Mood: A mood that is abnormally high, euphoric, and full of unmotivated happiness and vitality.
subtypes.Irritable Mood: A state where one gets angry or aggressive even at minor stimuli.
subtypes.Mood Lability: Rapid shifts in mood, alternating unpredictably between euphoria and irritability.

S034.name: Increased_Activity
S034.description: Abnormally and persistently increased goal-directed activity or energy.

subtypes.Increased Energy: Overflowing physical and mental energy, leading to an inability to stay still and a desire to keep moving.
subtypes.Hyperactivity: Doing far more work than usual or starting multiple activities simultaneously.
subtypes.Psychomotor Agitation: Inability to tolerate resting or stopping, driven by a constant need to do something.

S035.name: Inflated_Self_Esteem
S035.description: Inflated self-esteem or grandiosity (may range from uncritical self-confidence to delusional proportions).

subtypes.Inflated Self-Confidence: Feeling capable of anything and believing that failure is impossible, unlike one's usual self.
subtypes.Overestimation of Abilities: Unrealistically assessing one's talents, knowledge, or abilities as superior.
subtypes.Grandiose Delusions: The false belief that one is a special and important person with a special mission or purpose.

S036.name: Decreased_Sleep
S036.description: Decreased need for sleep (e.g., feels rested after only 3 hours of sleep).

subtypes.Reduced Sleep Duration: Sleeping significantly less than usual but feeling refreshed rather than tired.
subtypes.Loss of Sleep Need: Not feeling the urge to sleep or the thought that sleep is necessary.
subtypes.Indifference to Insomnia: Feeling no problem and continuing activities despite staying up for several nights.

S037.name: Pressured_Speech
S037.description: More talkative than usual or pressure to keep talking.

subtypes.Talkativeness: Speaking far more than usual and continuing to talk without rest.
subtypes.Rapid Speech: Speech speed is so fast that it is difficult for others to understand or interrupt.
subtypes.Pressured Speech: Cannot stop talking or tolerate silence due to an internal pressure to keep speaking.

S040.name: Increased_Goal_Activity
S040.description: Increase in goal-directed activity (at work, school, socially, or sexually) or purposeless psychomotor agitation.

subtypes.Occupational Hyperactivity: Driving significantly more projects or work than usual in the workplace or academic setting.
subtypes.Social Hyperactivity: Becoming much more sociable and extroverted than usual, actively meeting and contacting people.
subtypes.Hypersexuality: Significantly increased interest in or activity regarding sex.
subtypes.Psychomotor Agitation: Purposeless non-goal-directed activity, such as pacing or hand-wringing, driven by an inability to sit still.

symptom.disease_info: Bipolar II disorder is characterized by a recurrent course of major depressive episodes and hypomanic episodes, with no history of full manic episodes. Hypomanic periods involve persistently elevated, expansive, or irritable mood and increased energy or activity that are observable by others but less severe than mania and do not cause marked functional impairment or psychosis. Depressive episodes typically dominate the long-term course and are often the main reason patients seek treatment, sometimes leading to misdiagnosis as unipolar depression. The condition frequently begins in adolescence or early adulthood, can be triggered or unmasked by psychosocial stressors or changes in sleep–wake patterns, and is distinguished from cyclothymic disorder by the presence of full syndromal depressive episodes and from bipolar I by the absence of manic episodes.

patient.stressor: Andre had been piecing together freelance tech‑music gigs and part‑time work while aiming for a stable digital media project‑management role, but a canceled long‑term contract and mounting bills pushed his household finances into a precarious state. His wife noticed that his long‑standing pattern of cycling between periods of intense, late‑night recording and ambitious project planning, and stretches when he barely touched his guitar or coding projects, had become more pronounced as the financial pressure grew. Over the three weeks leading up to his clinic visit, he swung from drafting elaborate spreadsheets for new ventures and talking excitedly about multiple side hustles to abandoning those plans and spending days lying on the couch, increasingly worried about money yet unable to engage with job applications or community work at the center. After they fell behind on rent and he missed a deadline for a promising internship because he couldn’t bring himself to follow through, his wife urged him to see a psychiatrist at the community health clinic, worried that these recurring mood shifts were undermining their financial stability and his ability to get back into the workforce.
patient.chief_complaint: “My sleep has been all over the place—some nights I’m up planning and working on music, and other nights I can’t sleep at all or I sleep half the day.”

S024.name: Depressed_Mood
S024.description: A state where a sad, empty, or hopeless mood persists.
S024.manifestation: Lately I wake up with this heavy, sinking feeling in my chest, like I’ve already failed before the day even starts, and I just lie there staring at the ceiling thinking my wife would be better off without me dragging us down like this.

S026.name: Weight_Appetite_Change
S026.description: Significant increase or decrease in appetite or weight.
S026.manifestation: Most days I either forget to eat until my wife brings me a plate because I just don’t care, or I end up mindlessly inhaling chips and takeout late at night when the anxiety about money spikes, so my weight’s been bouncing around a bit.

S027.name: Sleep_Disturbance
S027.description: A state where there is a significant change in the quantity or quality of sleep.
S027.manifestation: Some nights I’m wired until four in the morning tweaking mixes and building these crazy detailed spreadsheets for new projects, and then other nights I just toss and turn thinking about the rent, or I crash so hard I sleep through half the day and miss emails and calls.

S028.name: Psychomotor_Changes
S028.description: Observable increase or decrease in psychomotor activity.
S028.manifestation: When I’m down, even getting up to shower feels like moving through mud and my wife says I shuffle around the apartment like a zombie, but when I’m in one of those high gears I’m pacing, drumming on every surface, and hopping from my laptop to my guitar to my phone without really stopping.

S031.name: Diminished_Thinking
S031.description: Diminished ability to think or concentrate, or indecisiveness.
S031.manifestation: I used to be sharp with code and arranging tracks, but these past few weeks my brain feels foggy—I'll stare at a job application for an hour, reread the same paragraph over and over, and still can’t decide what to write or even which position to click on.

S033.name: Elevated_Irritable_Mood
S033.description: A distinct period of abnormally and persistently elevated, expansive, or irritable mood.
S033.manifestation: There are stretches where I feel oddly amped and on edge at the same time—like I’m talking a mile a minute about all these ideas and then snapping at my wife over tiny things, like her asking about the budget, because any little question suddenly feels like an attack.

S034.name: Increased_Activity
S034.description: Abnormally and persistently increased goal-directed activity or energy.
S034.manifestation: On the higher days I have this restless energy where I can’t just sit and watch a show; I’m reorganizing my hard drives, sketching out three different business plans, messaging people about collaborations, and jumping between tasks like I’m racing some invisible clock.

S035.name: Inflated_Self_Esteem
S035.description: Inflated self-esteem or grandiosity (may range from uncritical self-confidence to delusional proportions).
S035.manifestation: When I get into those up phases, I catch myself thinking, ‘If I just focus for a week I can build an app, launch a YouTube channel, and fix our money problems overnight,’ like I’ve got some special grind mode other people don’t have, even though my track record says otherwise.

S036.name: Decreased_Sleep
S036.description: Decreased need for sleep (e.g., feels rested after only 3 hours of sleep).
S036.manifestation: During those bursts I’ll sleep three, maybe four hours, wake up before my alarm buzzing with ideas, and feel totally fine, like sleep is just an inconvenience that gets in the way of me knocking out all these projects.

S037.name: Pressured_Speech
S037.description: More talkative than usual or pressure to keep talking.
S037.manifestation: My wife keeps telling me to slow down because on those up days I’ll start talking about a new freelance plan and, before she can respond, I’ve already jumped to the next idea and the next story, barely taking a breath and not really letting her get a word in.

S040.name: Increased_Goal_Activity
S040.description: Increase in goal-directed activity (at work, school, socially, or sexually) or purposeless psychomotor agitation.
S040.manifestation: In the last few weeks I’ve had days where I suddenly decide I’m going to overhaul our whole life—sign up for three online courses, redesign my portfolio, reach out to everyone I’ve ever worked with—and I start all of it at once, staying busy nonstop but not actually finishing much.

add_requirements.functional_impairment: Because of these ups and downs, I’ve blown past application deadlines, lost track of bills, and pulled back from friends and stuff at the community center, so it feels like I’m stuck in place while our money situation keeps getting worse.
add_requirements.duration: Looking back, I’ve been cycling through these higher-energy spurts and heavy, shutdown lows on and off since my early twenties, but it’s gotten more noticeable and disruptive over the past few years as I’ve tried to get a steady job.
add_requirements.depressive_episode_duration: This current low stretch has been hanging over me for around three months, ever since that long-term contract fell through and I started feeling like I couldn’t get myself moving again.
